review_role: Independent actual saved-media inspection and lightweight saved-data cross-check; not a new mathematical audit
visual_findings: Actual x1 panel identifies the solid body, third medium, left attached support, five input averaging nodes and five right output measurement nodes. The external legend does not cover the structure.

The five output nodes are visible as purple open diamonds at source x=80 mm,y=28..30 mm even though the output spring is zero. They denote measurement nodes, not force arrows or prescribed individual motion.
Attached support uses filled black triangles; input averaging nodes use orange circles. Separate input-node curves show five unequal ux values and the common weighted mean.

Separate R and q_out axes avoid dual-axis ambiguity. Input-displacement axes use micrometres, R uses N, and the numeric panel uses mm/N. Gripper output is +y, physical mean uy=q_out, without a second sign flip.
Both the final PNG and each real GIF frame state that the stored original 0.025 mm task remains pending. Only the requested [0,0.001] mm prefix is marked reached.

Main geometry and force arrows use actual x1 coordinates. The supplementary displacement x1000 panel is explicitly labelled and has no force arrows. Its visible deformation is a magnified view of the same saved state.

PNG solid/medium J colour scales show their actual narrow ranges without a +1 offset; all element means are coloured and reported minimum uses all saved quadrature values. J is explicitly not pressure.

GIF contains only the two actual accepted states, in order, each lasting 1000 ms; no interpolated state is presented. Frame zero has zero force and motion; final frame displays the saved positive-y output.
Force arrows share one N scale across the complete accepted path and support/input/spring components. All attached-support arrows are included; other fixed-node reactions use the declared stride 3.
nonblocking_display_limits: At the actual x1 scale the maximum saved displacement is about 0.00136 mm on an 80 mm domain and is visually small; the labelled x1000 supplement is needed to inspect motion.

Adjacent 0.5 mm port markers and four support triangles are tightly grouped. The group and five output diamonds are visible, but every overlapping input/support/force glyph cannot be individually distinguished at the displayed size; metadata and CSV retain exact node identities and values.

Many other fixed-node reactions are small under the common force scale, and those reactions are displayed at stride 3. This is a display sample, not a claim that all reaction arrows are separately visible.
The five input-node curves lie close together at this prefix. Their unequal values are numerically retained; visual separation is limited without a local curve zoom.

GIF uses a shared indexed palette and has no numeric J colour bars; the PNG and metadata provide exact J ranges. Palette quantization and dense native-cell raster edges can affect visual colour detail.
The straight line between two plotted samples is a connection between saved observations and does not demonstrate any uncomputed intermediate equilibrium.
